Q: CRC32 MPEG-2 Algorithm Implementation on FPGA A:

If I understood correctly, since CRC's nature requiring XOR gates there is really nothing much to do to reduce resource usage other changing input data width say 32 to 8.

I could use LUT/ROMs to store 8 bit CRC32 results and then I could shift right and XOR 32 bit that requires 32x256 entry LUT. That requires 128 LUT6 If I'm not mistaken and that's pretty much higher than original algorithm.

Q: I need to create a 3-column hierarchical table A:

Since you wanted a solution for any number n, then if your example is given as:

A1=72
A2=36
A3=36

then you are only dealing with n=1 and should only be using A2:A27 for the input to the formula that I provided, but it's hard to show a 3-column hierarchical table using just those three values.

That brings up another point. I think most people would interpret the table below as having two different values in the first column, A1 and A2. Four different B values and 12 different C values. What is shown in the table are value labels, not range A1Notations and they aren't variable names.

If you want to represent duplicate values, you should use the same label, such as multiple C1s. Don't use A2=36 and A3=36 as an example of duplicate values.

Better yet, use different labels that don't look like range notations. For example, Item1, Item2 or real names/real numbers.

Q: How to maintain login session across multiple tabs? A:

It's not rocket science it's very simple just store the session token in http cookie so it's safe and simple so you can access that token from any tab! and there are multiple ways to handle the login flow you can use single auth token or access token and refresh token, so in this flow the refresh token will be store in http cookie and access token in state so from server when you send a req it'll look for refresh token and using that refresh token generate access token and store it in state and after that send that access token in header with every request!

Q: Where should SaveChanges() reside- in Unit of Work or in Generic repository? A:

If you have really complex needs, then that advice offers a way to do it, but don't do it specifically for mocking. The problem with mocking at the custom repo layer is that you won't be effectively testing the EF implementation or resolution of LINQ expressions to SQL.

If you do implement UoW over the top of EF (that is already UoW) then it is still important to do full integration testing, so the reality is that you are adding complexity to the implementation and the testing as well as adding more points of failure in your logic.

In most cases especially with micro-services it is better to keep things simple. If you are asking these questions then it is an indication you are optimising your solution prematurely.

Q: KQL Script to check existence of a file on Azure VM file system A:

You can use Azure Change Tracking and Inventory. It has option to add paths to files. It will monitor for changes to these files. In case you do not have changes there is inventory which runs once 24 hours and should list you the file. For example,

ConfigurationData 
| where ConfigDataType == "Files"
| where FileSystemPath == "C:\\Windows\\System32\\drivers\\etc\\hosts"

this one gets the inventory data for specific file that is under monitoring. If there is no record for specific server/vm for specific file that file does not exist on the server.

Keep in mind that Azure Change Tracking and Inventory contains several functionalities in it so if you want to exclude other functionalities you will have to change the Data collection rule. The UI only allows certain modifications.
